name: HAYUYA Mobile Portability Knowledge Base
intent: Machine-readable rules for deriving portable mobile/game assets from a source-faithful hero master. These are portability budgets and capability notes, not claims of universal engine hard limits.

portability_definition.principle: A portable asset is one that can be transformed into tiered runtime derivatives without destroying the high-quality master, and whose runtime forms respect scene-level performance, memory, bandwidth and thermal budgets.

universal_rules.portable_distribution_texture_container: KTX2 + Basis Universal when target runtime supports KHR_texture_basisu

compatibility.intent: Broad lower-end mobile compatibility; prioritize sustained 30 FPS and low bandwidth.
compatibility.lighting_bias: baked/static, one dominant dynamic light only when needed
compatibility.notes: HAYUYA house budget, not an engine hard limit.

balanced.intent: Mainstream mobile quality; sustained 30-60 FPS depending device and scene.
balanced.lighting_bias: baked/hybrid with tightly bounded dynamic lights and shadows
balanced.notes: HAYUYA house budget, not an engine hard limit.

high.intent: High-end mobile; preserve close-range fidelity while remaining scalable.
high.lighting_bias: hybrid/dynamic selectively; shadow distance and quality must scale
high.transparency_bias: budget by screen coverage and overdraw
high.notes: HAYUYA house budget, not an engine hard limit.

flagship.intent: Flagship mobile / showcase quality. Requires device profiling and fallback tiers.
flagship.recommended_astc_block: 5x5 or 4x4 selectively; 6x6 for less critical maps
flagship.lighting_bias: advanced mobile renderer allowed but must have lower tiers
flagship.notes: HAYUYA house budget, not an engine hard limit. 8K belongs to source/hero or exceptional use, not blanket runtime use.

lod_policy.material_rule: preserve appearance using shared PBR transfer/bakes; do not create extra material slots per LOD
lod_policy.rig_rule: do not simplify rigged meshes unless joints/weights are preserved and validated

engine_profiles.renderer: Mobile Forward / Mobile Deferred; experimental/beta desktop-renderer paths on select mobile
notable_mobile_limits: standard mobile renderer: no Nanite
no TSR
no hardware ray tracing
no Path Tracer
no Virtual Shadow Maps
no Lumen GI/reflections on standard mobile path
public_numeric_guidance: <=700 scene draw calls per single view
~700 draw-call target Galaxy Tab S6; <500 lower-end
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Do not interpret scene budgets as a per-asset cap. Keep material IDs low, build LOD/HLOD, and preserve a separate hero master.

engine_profiles.renderer: URP Forward / Forward+ / Deferred with Render Graph
notable_mobile_limits: Deferred has higher mobile performance impact than Forward/Forward+ in current URP docs
feature cost is device/content dependent
mobile remains bandwidth/overdraw/thermal sensitive
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Shared materials, instancing-friendly assets, LODs, ASTC/ETC2 variants and scalable texture/shader tiers.

engine_profiles.renderer: Mobile renderer (modern APIs) plus Compatibility renderer for older/lower-end devices; Forward+ for higher-end/desktop-class use
notable_mobile_limits: realtime lights/shadows/GI can be too expensive on low-power mobile
transparent rendering/overdraw is costly
automatic instancing behavior differs by renderer
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Keep opaque, instanceable, LOD-ready meshes and provide baked-lighting-friendly UV/material structure.

notable_mobile_limits: transparent instances in a batch may sort incorrectly
non-uniform scale can produce inaccurate normals in instancing path
dynamic batching has animation/content restrictions
public_numeric_guidance: docs recommend ASTC 6x6 for high-quality model textures as a practical preset
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Generate LODs, uniform-scale-safe normals, instancing-friendly variants and compressed texture packs.

notable_mobile_limits: draw calls remain expensive
hardware texture sampler limits vary
CPU skinning fallback reduces instancing opportunities
built-in glTF PBR lighting model is not supplied automatically
public_numeric_guidance: project setting can split meshes above 65,536 vertices for compatibility paths
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Prefer simple material contracts, few draw calls, portable GLB and compressed textures.

notable_mobile_limits: browser memory and power constraints
instance culling behavior must be considered
device pixel ratio can multiply fill/bandwidth cost
public_numeric_guidance: rough low-end mobile target: 100-200 draw calls
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Strongly minimize material/mesh splits and texture memory; keep web-ready compressed variants.

engine_profiles.renderer: Atom modular pipelines; low-end pipeline is default for iOS/Android
notable_mobile_limits: desktop/main pipeline should not be assumed portable; mobile defaults to low-end pipeline
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Keep the asset renderer-agnostic and provide low-end material/LOD variants.

notable_mobile_limits: draw-call and content density costs
quality level is device-dependent and not a stable numeric asset contract
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Identical reusable meshes/textures, low material variety, scalable geometric detail.

engine_profiles.renderer: Vulkan-centric mobile path with scalable graphics quality
notable_mobile_limits: advanced desktop-like effects need aggressive per-device scaling
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Provide ASTC-ready textures, mip/quality groups and renderer-neutral LODs.

notable_mobile_limits: mobile documentation is less prescriptive/current than Unreal/Unity/Godot; do not use as primary budget authority
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Use conservative GLB/PBR/LOD conventions rather than engine-specific assumptions.

engine_profiles.renderer: historical Android/Vulkan/GLES support in CRYENGINE 5.x documentation
portable_features: 32-bit index-buffer work and mobile Vulkan support appeared in 5.x
notable_mobile_limits: current public mobile guidance is comparatively stale; not a primary 2026 portability authority
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Track for compatibility knowledge only, not for modern default budgets.

graphics_apis: platform-specific; public filing does not expose a stable API contract
notable_mobile_limits: no public universal per-asset polygon/draw-call ceiling
production limits remain game/device specific
public_numeric_guidance: Ace Racer public GDC production talk: high-quality realistic graphics at 90fps
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Treat 90fps/high-fidelity mobile as possible on tuned content, but keep all Hayuya fallback tiers; do not infer proprietary engine internals that NetEase has not published.

engine_profiles.renderer: GameMaker renderer; primarily 2D but supports surfaces/3D graphics and Android GPU targeting
notable_mobile_limits: texture swaps and texture-page VRAM matter
24-bit screen color can cost performance
large-resolution/3D projects should target GPU-capable devices
public_numeric_guidance: official Android guidance suggests 1024x1024 texture pages when uncertain because of Android fragmentation
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Useful compatibility reference for texture-page/VRAM discipline, not a high-end 3D quality authority.

engine_profiles.renderer: WebGPU/WebGL browser renderer with growing 3D model support
notable_mobile_limits: fill rate can dominate on mobile
multitexturing trades CPU texture-switch cost for per-pixel GPU work
browser/mobile GPU capability varies
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Keep fill-rate, texture switching, effects and screen coverage conservative for browser-mobile variants.

notable_mobile_limits: developer owns most batching/material/LOD policy
API feature floor changes between GLES2 and GLES3
iOS OpenGL ES path is legacy/experimental in its current docs
engine_profiles.asset_implication: Use conservative GLB/PBR-derived content and explicit low-feature variants; do not assume an engine-managed scalability system.

engine_profiles.renderer: Cross-platform C# framework rather than a full content-scalability engine
notable_mobile_limits: developer is responsible for draw batching, LOD, material complexity, streaming and quality tiers
engine_profiles.asset_implication: HAYUYA should export neutral meshes/textures and metadata rather than depend on engine-side automatic optimization.

notable_mobile_limits: no engine safety net; developer owns CPU/GPU synchronization, draw submission, resource lifetime, memory, thermal adaptation and device compatibility
vendor/generation bottlenecks vary substantially
public_numeric_guidance: Vulkan lowers driver/draw-call overhead versus OpenGL ES in draw-heavy scenes; no universal draw-call/triangle ceiling
engine_profiles.asset_implication: HAYUYA output must be explicit and auditable: LOD chain, texture tiers, material count, collision, scale/orientation, compression plan and runtime budget metadata.

lessons: PBR/high-resolution textures create heavy CPU/GPU workload
scale target FPS before thermal throttling
public_large_game_case_studies.reported_result: Samsung case study reports ~7% higher average FPS and ~2C average / 3C max lower temperature in its tested BR battles.

lessons: same material across LODs to reduce shader switches
support hardware from entry-level to latest
1080p60 shipped target requires engine-level specialization and scalability
public_large_game_case_studies.reported_result: GDC 2023 session describes shipping 1080p 60fps while targeting varied hardware.

lessons: peak FPS is not sustained FPS
quality scalers should map to game-specific settings
thermal headroom must influence resolution/view distance/post and other fidelity
public_large_game_case_studies.reported_result: Google case study: 60fps test on Pixel 6 fell to 32fps after thermal pressure without adaptability; game-specific ADPF tuning sustained a much more stable result.

public_large_game_case_studies.engine_or_stack: Gameloft proprietary stack + Android Game Mode
lessons: battery mode can remove expensive reflection/ray-tracing, DoF and simplify motion blur/weather shaders
high-end mobile can support very high refresh and selected ray-tracing effects
these are flagship paths, not baseline portability requirements
public_large_game_case_studies.reported_result: Tencent GDC 2024 schedule documents sessions on 144 FPS mobile rendering and mobile ray tracing.

android.legacy_api: OpenGL ES remains supported but not primary for new graphics features
android.thermal_rule: measure thermal headroom and adapt before severe throttling
android.memory_rule: use Memory Advice / engine telemetry where possible; do not assume one RAM budget across devices

ios.architecture_rule: Apple GPUs use tile-based deferred rendering; minimize render-target/system-memory round trips
ios.memory_rule: memory limits are device-dependent; excessive use can trigger termination
ios.texture_rule: ASTC is broadly relevant on Apple GPU families; select formats by target capability

common_tile_gpu.rule: Keep transient/deferred data on-chip when engine/API supports it; avoid unnecessary stores/loads and render passes.
common_tile_gpu.why: External memory bandwidth costs performance and power on tile-based mobile GPUs.

rules: Keep opaque work friendly to hidden-surface removal.
Avoid unnecessary system-memory stores/loads for transient attachments.
Treat discard/alpha-test and layered transparency as architecture-sensitive costs.
Keep temporary deferred data on-chip where the renderer/API permits.
powervr.why: PowerVR documentation describes bandwidth/power savings from tile memory and hidden-surface removal; mobile efficiency depends strongly on minimizing system-memory traffic.

vendors: PowerVR and other Vulkan/OpenGL ES implementations
cross_vendor_android.rule: Never infer one GPU's bottleneck from another. Profile CPU and GPU frame time on real vendor hardware; vendor and generation differences can materially change bottlenecks.
cross_vendor_android.geometry: Use LOD, culling and mesh simplification when geometry is the actual bottleneck.
cross_vendor_android.shaders: Use the lowest adequate precision and avoid needless passes/attachments.
cross_vendor_android.textures: Use GPU compression and mipmaps; ASTC primary on modern Android with fallback packaging.

zombie_game_asset_rules.crowd_zombies: Use shared skeletons/materials where possible, animation LOD/update throttling, mesh LODs and instancing/batching-compatible materials.
zombie_game_asset_rules.hero_zombie: Allow higher LOD0 and richer material detail, but retain lower LODs and cheaper shadow/material variants.
zombie_game_asset_rules.gore_transparency: Prefer geometry/decals/masks with controlled screen coverage; uncontrolled translucent layers are high-risk for overdraw.
zombie_game_asset_rules.environment: Favor modular reusable meshes, shared atlases/materials, occlusion-friendly layout, HLOD/impostors for distance, baked/hybrid lighting.
zombie_game_asset_rules.props: Keep material slots low and collapse tiny geometric detail into normal/detail maps only when that is cheaper for the target tier.
zombie_game_asset_rules.collision: Generate simplified convex/simple collision; render mesh is not the collision budget.
zombie_game_asset_rules.textures: Keep 8K at hero/source level unless a flagship runtime test proves it justified; derive 4K/2K/1K tier variants with mipmaps and mobile compression.

coverage.scope: Major current 3D-capable mobile engines, mobile-first runtimes, web-mobile 3D stacks, large proprietary production engines with public evidence, and mobile GPU/platform constraints.
coverage.rationale: There are thousands of niche, internal and abandoned engines. Hayuya tracks engines that materially change a 3D mobile asset contract, plus large-company internal engines when credible public technical evidence exists.

texture_delivery.strategy: Physical KTX2/Basis Universal embedded in runtime GLBs with KHR_texture_basisu; engine build systems may transcode to native ASTC/ETC2 as appropriate.

codec_policy.high_fidelity_linear_maps: UASTC for normalTexture, occlusionTexture and metallicRoughnessTexture

native_gpu_formats.note: Do not mislabel Basis Universal payloads as pre-transcoded ASTC/ETC2. Native GPU format selection may happen at runtime or during engine-specific build packaging.
